attempted_claim: Let (G,P) be a relatively hyperbolic pair such that G is one-ended and has a finite-index subgroup with no 2-torsion, the Bowditch boundary M=∂(G,P) is connected, planar, has no cut point, and contains an embedded Sierpiński carpet, and G is virtually compact special (in particular, G acts properly and cocompactly on a CAT(0) cube complex with virtually special peripheral intersections in the compatible sense of Groves–Manning). Is G virtually Kleinian, i.e. does a finite-index subgroup of G admit a faithful geometrically finite representation into Isom(H^3)?
decisive_failure: Three concrete routes (JSJ plus carpet rigidity, RACG counterexample search, hierarchy to 3-manifold promotion) were attempted with a bounded computational recovery test; all terminate at the same carpet-case modulus and rigid-vertex gap. No independently valuable original increment survived Audit reassessment, and no preset fallback exists for this target-only topic.
